DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE ANO LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, west Triangle, Quezon City http:/_/www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 79 s. 2021 11 June 2021 ATTY. BRYAN LLOYD L. DELA ROSA ATTY. PAUL VINCENT M. CASILLA Dela Rosa Casilla Law Office 3rd Floor, Power Realty Building 1012 Arnaiz Street, San Lorenzo Makati City Dear Atty. Dela Rosa: This has reference to your letter dated 19 February 2021 requesting this Department's opinion on whether the Local Government of Malabon City can require payment of tax assessment duly appealed in the Regional Trial Court pursuant to the Local Government Code of 1991 as a pre- requisite for the application for renewal of business permit of Fransix Co., Inc. Foremost, please be informed that Department is an agency under the executive branch of the government and as such, it has no authority to declare invalid any ordinance or resolution of the local sanggunians, or any act committed by local officials thereof which is alleged to be in violation of the Local Government Code or other applicable laws. Only the courts have the authority to do so upon initiation of the appropriate action. Moreover, this Department is proscribed, under our internal rules as provided in Memorandum Circular No. 2010-02, to act on queries of the foå\owing kinds, to Wit: 3. Those that are litis pendencia. or pending litigation except when the COUtt itself requests for the opinion. xxx; 4. Those ihai are coqnizabie bv other agencies of the government.

Considering that the herein case is currently pending in court, the arguments you have propounded should be threshed out in the proper forum. for Of acauen¯tiC uiSCUSSiOfi the on whether an LGU can require payment of tax assessment duly appealed the RTC pursuant to the LGC as a pre-requisite for the application for renewal of business permit of corporation, allow us to cite the decision rendered by the Court of Appeals (CA), having the same issue as herein propounded. In the case of Synovate Inc. vs Pasig City Mayor Robeno C. Eusebio, et.al, one of the issues answered by the CA is whether or not the refusal of respondents Mayor and BPLO to issue business permits to petitioner has legal basis. The CA has ruled that: "As regards the refusal of respondents to issue a business permit, petitioner posits that such refusal without prior payment of the 2004 Assessment is tantamount to a disregard or petitioners right to protest the assessment. Petitioner likewise contends that Section 77(b) of the Pasig Revenue Code of 1992 is invalid for being contrary to the provisions of the LGC According to petitioner, as stated by the OLOF-DO' its opinion, Section 174 of the LGC specifies the remedies of a local govemment unit in the collection of local taxes and withholding of business permit is not among such remedies and thus, said Section 77(d) is null and void for being ultra vires. Petitioner's contentions are specious. For easy reference, Section 77(d) of Pasig Revenue Code of 1992 (Pasig Ordinance No. 25, Series of 1992, as amended) provides as follows: "d) Mayor's Permit may not be issued to any person, partnersmp and/or corporation who; wojated any Ordinance or Regulation relative to permit and license granted, failed to pay the tax or fee of business discovered operating without a license, and fails to pay the fine, penalty, basic tax or other liabilities from niisdeclaration an underdeclaration of the taxable receipts/sales WiÜiiii (SO) days frOjii [he o' ihe deriiåiid. ('Eiiiphases supplied) This Coutt will not be hasty in declaring a tax ordinance invalid or illegal, as it is mindful of the well-etched dictum by the Supreme Coutt in people vs. Vera-' that: "A becoming Of inferior courts demands conscious realization of the position that they occupy in the interrelation and operation of the integrated judicial system of the nation." Especially so, the power to determine any question on the legality of tax ordinances, such as the Pasig Revenue Code of 1992, is not within the province of this Court hut is primarily lodged on the

Secretary of Justice, pursuant to Section 187 of the LGC of 1991, and under cenain conditions, is vested with the courts of general jurisdiction or the Regional Trial Coutts. It must be emphasized that this COUN is a coun of special jurisdiction and can only take cognizance of such matters as are clearly within its jurisdiction. The Pasig Revenue Code of 1992, including Section 77(d) thereof, enjoys the presumption of validity, unless declared othetwise. There being no contrary declaration, respondent Mayor has the duty, inter alia, to '(e)nsure that all taxes and other revenues of the city are collected" and '(i)ssue licenses and permits and suspend or revoke the same tor any violation ot tne conditions upon which said licenses or permits had been issued, pursuant to law or ordinance" Furthermore, Section 3.05 of the Malabon City Ordinance No. A10-2016 states that: "A Mayor's Permit shall not be issued to: I. Any person who previously violated an ordinance or regulation goveming permits granted; 2. Any person whose business establishment or undenaking does not conform with zoning regulations, and safety, health and other requirements of the municipality; 3. Any person who has unsettled tax obligation, debt or other liability to the govemment. " Be that as it may, this opinion shall be without prejudice to the decision/opinion that will be rendered by the courts/ agency that is more authoritative on the matter. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: GAN Under ecretary for Local Government LS,90/17 Copy furnished: DIR. MARIA LOURDES L.
